title: Hosted endpoints: tiered traffic controls & quality gates blueprint
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket is the authoritative product blueprint for a tiered traffic control and quality-gating system applied to the hosted inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). The goal is to enable predictable behavior and cost isolation across lanes (free/standard/premium) while protecting user-visible quality and allowing progressive rollouts based on eval signals and telemetry.
background: Customers expect predictable latency and quality guarantees as they scale. Current hosted lanes expose a single surface that makes it hard to: 1) apply per-lane throttles and cost limits, 2) gate rollouts by quality regressions, and 3) provide clear UIs for SLA tiers. Engineering has prototyped lane-aware routing and per-tenant throttles; this blueprint consolidates requirements, acceptance criteria, and the rollout safety net.
goals: 1) Define lane semantics (free/standard/premium) for traffic shaping and cost caps. 2) Specify eval-driven quality gates to block rollouts or auto-rollback for perceptible regressions. 3) Provide operational playbook (canary slices, telemetry checks, fallback policies). 4) Ensure compatibility with Dedicated and Private routing policies.
out_of_scope: Dedicated private control plane implementation, on-prem installer packaging, UI redesign of billing console beyond displaying lane attribution. Low-level kernel selection/quantization tuning is handled by ENG-20590.
success_metrics:
- Percent of production requests with lane attribution metadata >= 99%
- No more than 1 customer-facing regression P1 per release attributable to model rollouts in first 2 weeks
- Cost delta for standard lane within +/- 10% of forecast after 30 days
- Eval gate false positive rate < 5% on held-out test suites
acceptance_criteria: 1) API: New request payload supports optional 'lane' header and server-side attribution when absent. 2) Routing: Requests assigned to lanes respect per-lane QPS and burst policies; enforced at p99. 3) Rollout control: A deploy can be bound to an eval suite and a threshold; if violations exceed threshold for two consecutive windows (5m each), automatic rollback triggers. 4) Telemetry: Console exposes lane-level latency/cost/quality (token-level cost attribution) with 1m resolution. 5) Backfill: Historical metrics must be reprocessed for past 72h for retroactive attribution. 6) Security: KMS-backed keys for any lane-specific crypto; security review signoff recorded. 7) Docs: SDKs and API docs updated with lane examples and migration notes.
scope_changes_and_clarifications:
- Initial intent included multi-protocol support (grpc + rest) on day-one; changed to REST-first for launch due to infra SDK compatibility (dependency ENG-19821). GRPC support scheduled in Phase 2.
- Deterministic seeding for 'standard' lane optional at launch; we will enable on a per-customer opt-in basis to avoid global variance.
- Ephemeral KV cache experiment removed from baseline rollout (moved to experimental flag) to avoid evict storms during canary traffic slices.
- Compact embeddings path for low-cost lane will use 8-bit quantization only after an eval pass; if regression > 3% on similarity benchmarks, fallback to full embeddings.
rollout_checklist:
Pre-launch:
- Complete ENG-19821 routing implementation and run internal throughput test (tolerance: <= 10% overhead)
- Create eval suites for generation, chat flow coherence, embeddings similarity, and rerank precision (owners: PM, Research)
- Security review signoff for KMS usage and lane metadata handling
- Create canary slices (1% traffic, diverse tenant sizes) and verify lane attribution on 100% of canary requests
- Documentation: API examples + migration guide published and linked
Canary phase:
- Activate canary for 3 days or 1M requests (whichever earlier)
- Monitor: p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost per request, eval suite pass rate every 5m
- Gate: if eval failure rate > 2% or user-facing errors spike > 0.5% absolute, pause and investigate
Gradual rollout:
- 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple cycles with health checks between steps
Post-launch:
- Backfill attribution for last 72h
- Run 14-day regression monitoring with alerts for quality regressions tied to eval suite metrics
- Quarterly review for lane pricing and cost model adjustments
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Eval suite misses real-world failure modes -> Mitigation: Add lightweight production probes that sample user interactions and run heuristics for hallucination and truncation.
Risk: Throttles cause customer SLA regressions -> Mitigation: Borrow Dedicated-style burst capacity hooks for high-paying tenants; set safe default bursts and provide customer opt-in.
Risk: Attribution overhead increases latency -> Mitigation: Implement attribution tagging asynchronously and provide fallbacks with eventual consistency for non-critical paths.
stakeholder_signoffs: PM: Maya Chen; Research: Dr. Elena Vargas; Eng infra: Rahul Mehta; Security: Priya Nair; Legal: Claire Dubois
open_questions:
1) Should lane billing attribution be emitted synchronously in the response header or only written to internal telemetry? (tradeoff: transparency vs added latency)
2) For multi-model fallbacks (e.g., quantized variant when premium model unavailable), should we preserve lane SLA guarantees or surface a lane-level degraded status to consumers?
3) How aggressive should automatic rollback sensitivity be to avoid thrashing on transient eval noise?
next_steps:
1) Align on synchronous vs async attribution decision in this review (owner: Adrian Patel)
2) ENG kickoff for REST routing + throttles (owner: Rahul Mehta)
3) Research to finalize eval suites and breakpoints by 2026-01-10
4) Security review initiated and KMS integration scoped (owner: Priya Nair)
notes: We intentionally decoupled GRPC and ephemeral KV cache from baseline to shorten time-to-value and reduce rollout blast radius. This blueprint also provides hooks for Dedicated and Private routing layers so customers moving to those modes will see consistent lane semantics.
